title: Correlation-assisted topological and metamagnetic transitions in Rashba-coupled superconductors: $t$-$J$-$U$ model study
authors: Tushar Dey, Maciej Fidrysiak, Józef Spałek
abstract: Unconventional superconductivity commonly emerges in systems characterized by strong electronic correlations, with layered copper-oxides serving as a canonical example. Observation of spin-momentum locking within Bi-family of the cuprates, compatible with the presence of non-negligible Rashba-type spin-orbit coupling (RSOC), calls for an investigation of the joint effects of electronic correlations and RSOC on pairing in copper-oxide and related superconductors. Employing statistically-consistent variational approximation (SGA), we carry out such an analysis by constructing the phase diagram for the case of square-lattice \textit{t-J-U} model incorporating RSOC. We also investigate the effects of time-reversal-symmetry breaking by Zeeman field, as well as characterize emergent topological superconducting (TSC) states. Chern number $C = \pm 4$ TSC is found in a broad regime of on-site Coulomb repulsion close to half-filling. The latter is not governed by correlations and emerges also within the weak-coupling Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) scheme. Yet, we identify a distinct $C = \pm 2$ TSC state that is driven specifically by electronic correlations via a topological transition occurring with no bulk quasiparticle gap closure, and is accompanied by discontinuous metamagnetic and Lifshitz transitions. Moreover, a qualitatively distinct doping evolution of the $d$- and $p$-wave components of the underlying mixed-parity SC order parameter above the metal-to-insulator transition is demonstrated. Our work points toward the relevance of joint correlation and RSOC effects beyond BdG scheme to phase diagrams of RSOC-coupled superconductors.
summary: This theoretical study examines how combining strong electronic correlations with Rashba spin-orbit coupling affects superconductivity in cuprate-like materials. Using the $t$-$J$-$U$ model, the authors pinpoint a correlation-driven topological superconducting state ($C=\pm 2$) that manifests alongside distinct metamagnetic transitions. The work highlights the necessity of correlation effects beyond mean-field theories to accurately map the phase diagram of such complex superconductors.
main_problem: The study investigates the joint effects of electronic correlations and Rashba-type spin-orbit coupling (RSOC) on superconducting pairing, focusing on emergent topological and metamagnetic transitions.
main_result: The authors identify a distinct $C = \pm 2$ Topological Superconducting (TSC) state driven specifically by electronic correlations, which is accompanied by discontinuous metamagnetic and Lifshitz transitions.
method: The analysis employs the Statistically-Consistent Variational Approximation (SGA) applied to the $t$-$J$-$U$ model, analyzing phase diagrams and free-energy differences.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using the $t$-$J$-$U$ Hamiltonian augmented with RSOC and a Zeeman field, applied to a square lattice structure relevant to cuprate superconductors.
key_observables: Chern number ($C$), SC order parameter components ($\Delta_d$, $\Delta_p$), magnetization, and the free-energy difference ($\Delta F$).
important_parameters: On-site Coulomb repulsion ($U$), RSOC magnitude ($V$), and Zeeman field ($h$) are varied across different doping regimes near half-filling.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the SGA approximation and restricts the variational space to maintain lattice translational symmetry, excluding long-range SDW or CDW orders.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the evolution of SC amplitudes, energy gaps, and magnetization as a function of band filling, showing hysteresis loops and transitions between different topological states ($C=\pm 4$ vs $C=\pm 2$).
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the phase diagram by varying correlation strength ($U$) and doping, comparing results obtained from the $t$-$J$-$U$ model against simpler weak-coupling schemes (BdG) to isolate correlation-driven physics.
why_interesting: The explicit inclusion of RSOC and its interaction with strong correlations provides a rich platform for studying topological superconductivity beyond standard BCS theory, which is relevant for understanding exotic superconducting phases in correlated materials.

FIG. 2. Reference results for spin-orbit coupling and Zeeman field set to zero (V ≡0, h ≡0). The panels show the band- filling dependence of the singlet d-wave order parameter, ∆d, as well as equal-spin triplet p-wave components, ∆↑↑ p+ and ∆↓↓ p− (here equal to zero, indicating pure d-wave SC). The on-site Coulomb interaction is set to (a) U = 6|t|, (b) U = 8|t|, (c) U = 10|t|, and (d) U = 14|t|. The remaining parameters are t = −0.35 eV, t′ = 0.25|t|, J = 0.3|t|, kBT = 10−5|t|, and lattice of size has been set to N = 800 × 800. Metal- to-insulator transition at the half filling (n = 1) occurs in between U = 10|t| and U = 14|t|, cf. panels (c) and (d).
